title: feat: simpler classifier, priority on every issue
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Follow-up to #15387.

- Every issue gets High / Medium / Low by user impact, team issues included; paying customers are raised to High, and people can still change it by hand
- One classify path and one answer format for issues and PRs (PR facts like changed files and linked issues are passed as extra input)
- `OUTAGE` folds into `BUG`: four types (`BUG`, `FEATURE`, `QUESTION`, `TRACKING`); priority carries the severity
- The AI no longer guesses app submissions; the form's `APP-SUBMISSION` label is enough
- Quest and news issues get labelled like any other issue; on issues the classifier never adds or removes `POLLEN-QUEST`
- Issues relayed from Discord count as people, not `AUTOMATED`
- The schema lists the eight kinds; the model had put a type in the kind field (#15368, #14086)

Dry run from this branch: quest/news issues labelled with `POLLEN-QUEST` untouched, relayed issues lose `AUTOMATED`, CI issues keep it.

gist.headline: Every issue gets a compass
gist.blurb: The issue gardener now gives every report a High, Medium, or Low priority, including the ones written by the people tending the garden. Fewer classifier side quests; more consistent labels.
gist.summary: Unified issue and PR classification into one schema-driven path, assigning High/Medium/Low priority to every issue, folding OUTAGE into BUG, preserving POLLEN-QUEST labels on issues, and correctly treating Discord-relayed reports as human submissions.
gist.impact: Maintainers get more consistent triage across BUG, FEATURE, QUESTION, and TRACKING issues, with customer reports elevated to High while manual priority choices remain intact.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy issue-triage garden: Polli acts as a careful gardener with a tiny clipboard, placing High, Medium, and Low signposts beside four healthy code-plants labeled BUG, FEATURE, QUESTION, and TRACKING. A small CRT monitor robot sorts friendly paper issue cards, while a preserved POLLEN-QUEST flower marker remains untouched, representing simpler and more reliable automation.
